title: A mosque founded on piety
hookLine: a mosque founded on mindfulness from the first day, with people who love to be clean (9:108)

lines: ONE BUILT ON WHAT YOU CAN'T SEE.
cards: Two buildings on the edge of Medina, both with a place to pray, both facing the same direction. From the street, you might not tell them apart.
One was built, the Qur'an says, to cause harm, to split the believers and to give cover to someone working against them. The other was built on something you can't see in the brickwork at all.
At-Tawbah tells the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ never to stand in the first one. And it points to the second, with a phrase about foundations that people have carried ever since.

teach.b: Verse one hundred seven describes a mosque set up to do damage and to divide; tradition calls it Masjid ad-Dirar, the mosque of harm. Verse one hundred eight says, in paraphrase: never stand in it.
A mosque founded on taqwa from the first day is more worthy for you to stand in. In it are people who love to purify themselves, and God loves those who purify themselves.

Taqwa is the word Pickthall renders here as duty to Allah, and others as piety or mindfulness: a constant awareness of God that shapes what you do. So a building can have a foundation under the foundation.

Some commentators say Quba, the mosque built when the Prophet reached the edge of Medina, just after the journey that began in the cave. A hadith in Muslim's collection has the Prophet naming his own mosque in Medina.
Scholars have held both, and some say the verse fits both. Then the cleanliness.

teach.h: PEOPLE WHO LOVE TO BE CLEAN.
teach.b: Commentators connect the people who love to purify themselves with the people of Quba, known for washing carefully with water.
A hadith reported by Ibn Majah and an-Nasa'i says that whoever purifies himself at home, then comes to Quba and prays there, has a reward like a lesser pilgrimage.

Inner and outer meet in one verse: a heart that's honest about why it built something, and hands that keep the place clean. Neither is an extra. The intention is the foundation; the cleaning is how you live in the house.

how: Visitors to Medina pray at the Quba mosque, some after making wudu first, following the hadith on its reward; volunteers in mosques around the world take turns cleaning the prayer hall and the washing area.

o: the ritual washing you do before each prayer
a constant awareness of God that shapes what you do
a careful, lifelong study of the books of law

p: the mosque built to cause harm

s: the verse names the mosque founded on piety
it doesn't. some say Quba; a hadith in Muslim names the Prophet's mosque; some say both.
the mosque of harm looked like any other mosque
the difference the verse names is the intention under the bricks.
cleanliness is mentioned in the same verse as piety
God loves those who purify themselves, right after the foundation of taqwa.

games.q: a group invites the Prophet to pray in their new mosque. it looks like any other. what does the Qur'an tell him?
o: pray there once, to keep the peace.
pray there, but don't stay long.
games.why: never stand in it: it was built to cause harm and division. a mosque founded on taqwa from the first day is more worthy.

practice: Think of a place you share with other people, a kitchen, an office, a prayer room, a stairwell, and picture the corner of it nobody takes care of. Then ask yourself the verse's quiet question: why do I do the things I do there?

wordCard.voice: Taqwa, piety, mindfulness, awareness of God. A mosque founded on it from the first day, and kept by people who love to be clean. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: piety, mindfulness, awareness of God; the foundation the verse names (9:108).

carryVoice: Your line: founded on piety. Intention first, then the bricks. See you at the next one.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 1398 (the mosque founded on taqwa is the Prophet's mosque)
Sunan Ibn Majah 1412; Sunan an-Nasa'i 699 (purifying at home and praying at Quba)
